arithmetic.method: Every elasticity identity is evaluated on random displacement jets over a prime field.  The jet of a displacement field is unconstrained, so a random jet probes the identity fully, and the sampling error is one-sided in exactly the same way as on the curvature side: a finite bank can only report the admissible space too LARGE.  It is closed from below by exhibiting the two Lame directions and re-verifying them on held-out jets.

basis_completeness_citations.citation: H. Weyl, The Classical Groups (1939), first fundamental theorem for O(n)
basis_completeness_citations.statement: Every O(n)-invariant tensor is a linear combination of products of Kronecker deltas.  For rank 4 that is exactly the three delta pairings this search enumerates, so the enumeration is complete for isotropic materials.  CITED, not derived here.

basis_completeness_citations.citation: A. L. Cauchy, Exercices de mathematiques 3 (1828) 160
basis_completeness_citations.statement: The isotropic linear elastic law is sigma_ij = lambda d_ij tr(eps) + 2 mu eps_ij, and the static equilibrium operator it forces is mu lap u + (lambda + mu) grad div u -- the Navier-Cauchy equation.  This is what the elasticity search re-derives.

basis_completeness_citations.citation: W. Voigt, Lehrbuch der Kristallphysik (1910), on the Cauchy relations
basis_completeness_citations.statement: The rari-constant reduction lambda = mu is an additional hypothesis, not a consequence, and it is contradicted by measurement.  Imposing it here shrinks the space from two constants to one, which the search reports as a relaxation control.

decision: DERIVED: with flat Euclidean 3-space, a displacement field, a rank-4 concomitant linear in the LINEAR STRAIN tensor, material isotropy and a symmetric Cauchy stress declared, the surviving space is exactly two-dimensional and is spanned by d_ij d_kl and d_ik d_jl + d_il d_jk -- the Lame constants lambda and mu.  The static equilibrium operator those force is d_j sigma_ij = (1 mu) lap u_i + (1 lambda + 1 mu) d_i (div u), the Navier-Cauchy equation.  This is the SAME engine that returns g_mn and R_mn - (1/2) R g_mn from the curvature declaration; the different answer comes from the different declaration, which is the point.

declared_framework.concomitant_class: linear in the linear strain tensor eps_ij = (d_i u_j + d_j u_i)/2, with constant coefficients built from the Kronecker delta alone
declared_framework.conservation_motivation: angular momentum balance forces the Cauchy stress to be symmetric; the existence of a strain-energy function forces the major symmetry of C
declared_framework.geometry: flat Euclidean d-space in Cartesian coordinates: the metric is the constant Kronecker delta, the connection and the Riemann tensor of that metric are computed and come out identically zero, and partial derivatives are covariant derivatives
declared_framework.machine_checkable_note: This sub-block is the part of the declaration the engine can confront with the computation. It SELECTS the basis generator -- concomitant_generator = linear_strain_tensor routes to the elasticity generator, riemann_tensor routes to the curvature generator -- and every field is then re-measured off the arrays that generator actually built. Any disagreement raises FrameworkMismatch and no receipt is sealed. The free-text keys below are prose for a reader and are never trusted. tensor_symmetry refers to the Cauchy stress the law produces, which is measured on the bank; the minor and major symmetries of the elasticity tensor itself are declared as CONSTRAINTS below, because whether they bind is a thing the search is supposed to find out.

how far the declared symmetries collapse that count
that the surviving space in d >= 2 is exactly two-dimensional

framework_consistency.what_this_closes: Before this gate the declared_framework block was inert: it was copied verbatim into the receipt and referenced nowhere in the computation, so a receipt could carry a framework claim describing a completely different theory from the one that produced its numbers.  Every field above is now MEASURED off the arrays the basis generator built -- the signature of the base-point metric, whether the sampled curvature is identically zero, the index structure of the primary field jet, the rank and pair symmetry of the produced terms, and which terms die on an exactly flat jet -- and a receipt is refused when any of them disagrees with what was declared.

dimension_sweep.question: is the count of two elastic constants a dimension-independent fact?
dimension_sweep.verdict: NO.  In d = 1 all three delta pairings coincide and a rod has ONE elastic constant; from d = 2 upward the count is exactly two.  The count is derived per dimension by the same enumeration, not carried over.

minor_symmetry_is_not_an_independent_dec.question: is the minor symmetry of the elasticity tensor an extra assumption, or is it forced by the symmetry of the Cauchy stress?
minor_symmetry_is_not_an_independent_dec.verdict: FORCED.  Declaring only that the Cauchy stress is symmetric -- angular momentum balance -- and letting the law contract the RAW displacement gradient still collapses the space onto the same two directions.  The minor symmetry did not need to be declared separately; it was already implied.

imposing_the_cauchy_relation_shrinks_the.reading: lambda = mu is the 19th-century rari-constant hypothesis.  It is an extra declaration, it collapses the space to a single constant, and it is contradicted by measurement -- so the search reports it as a constraint that costs a dimension, not as a result.

reused_repository_machinery.use: Cross-check of the curvature engine against an independent implementation: the repository's own sympy Schwarzschild Ricci computation is Ricci-flat, and the jet engine must agree that a Ricci-flat metric has vanishing Einstein tensor.

The contracted Bianchi identity nabla^a G_ab = 0 that makes the divergence-free constraint bite is already an established repository control.  It is hash-bound here and independently re-derived on the metric-jet bank, so the search does not lean on an unchecked import.

Varying the Einstein-Hilbert action is the complementary route to the same tensor.  Hash-bound as the control that this constraint search reproduces by a different method: no action is postulated here, only constraints.
Declared Einstein-Hilbert action spec the variation control is registered against.
The repository's surviving screened-gravity candidates.  Bound so the relaxation control can state exactly which declaration axis they live on.
Float-rejecting canonical serialization used for every seal in this receipt.

scope: One declared framework (flat Euclidean space with a displacement field), one declared concomitant class (rank-4, constant-coefficient, linear in the linear strain), one declared material symmetry (isotropy) and four declared dimension cells.  That the delta pairings exhaust the O(n)-invariant rank-4 tensors is Weyl's first fundamental theorem, CITED and not derived.  Nothing here is novel: Cauchy (1828) and Navier (1821) are the mathematics.  No observational data is opened.
